runtime_requirements.why: The exerciser opens /csd-exerciser-target with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC and write(2)s a byte every cycle, so trace_open records a write-intent open continuously post-attach. Unlike the cap gate, no sysctl is needed — the write fires regardless. The container declares no volumes, so the file's parent (/) is an unbacked rootfs write and the recommendation reports read_only:true with / as a tmpfs candidate.

notes: Synthetic regression fixture for the v0.2 read-only-filesystem observer, the fs analog of expected.json. Role: prove that when a userspace process performs write-intent opens post-attach, `csd --observe fs` records the path. `csd --observe fs --container <synthetic>` must produce a writable_paths entry whose path is /csd-exerciser-target (disposition tmpfs_candidate, since the container has no volume covering /). This is the sole deterministic fs gate: postgres/caddy/tailscale can legitimately observe zero post-attach writes (their writes happen pre-attach, at container/entrypoint init), the same workload-shape caveat docs/known-deltas.md records for caps. Confidence grades low by design (sparse single-path observation), so this run is never a contributable profile — it is a pipeline attach+record regression check only.
